comparison: Perfect agreement on automated behavioral detection (C3, C4). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes strong mAP (0.97) but mentions lack of quantitative human validation; peer reviewers praised this as 'exceptional methodological advance' without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on social face distractor effects (C5, C6, C7). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate statistics and substantial effect sizes but cautions about small sample size (n=4); peer reviewers accepted findings as 'convincing' without challenge.

Agreement on in-group/out-group discrimination (C12, C13, C73, C74). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes strong control analysis (C13) but notes small sample and one non-significant monkey; peer reviewers accepted findings without challenging statistical robustness.

Divergent evaluations on modeling approach (C14-C19, C31). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with technical concerns about discrete grid optimization; peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, expressing confusion about weight interpretation and asking whether in-group effects could be tested.

Agreement on selective oxytocin effects on out-group attention (C23-C26). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes lack of placebo blinding and potential order effects; peer reviewers accepted findings as 'important' without raising methodological concerns.

Divergent evaluations on oxytocin effects on SEI (C27-C30). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED despite marginal significance (p=0.03) and small sample; peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning reliability and consistency of weights across conditions.

Agreement on dyadic relationship findings (C32-C34). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for IEI analysis showing aggression dominance; peer reviewers also SUPPORTED, with editor highlighting dyadic relationships as important findings. OpenEval R9 covers oxytocin effects on dyadic aggression (C35-C37) which peer R7 also addresses and supports.

Agreement on oxytocin amplifying dyadic aggression effects (C35-C37, C54). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes reasonable interpretation but speculative mechanism; peer reviewers accepted findings about oxytocin altering dyadic relationships without specific concerns.

Partial overlap on methodological claims (C1, C2). OpenEval rates basic methods as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN primarily due to sample size concerns (C78), which OpenEval addresses separately in R11.

Agreement on sample size limitation (C78). Both acknowledge this as a significant constraint. OpenEval rates limitations as appropriately identified (SUPPORTED); peer reviewers express UNCERTAIN about generalizability, with Reviewer 2 explicitly stating small sample 'limits the generalizability of the findings.'

Agreement on basic distractor effects (C10, C11). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval includes these in broader analysis of social face effects; peer Reviewer 1 praised 'Well-designed and robust experiments' linking lab tasks to spontaneous behaviors.

Agreement on familiarization procedure (C9). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this as part of in-group/out-group discrimination evidence; peer Reviewer 2 accepted familiarization protocol while noting concerns about limited stimulus set.

Agreement on control analysis specificity (C20). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this strengthens specificity claims in modeling approach; peer reviewers accepted overall experimental design as robust without challenging this control.

Partial overlap on high-level summaries (C39, C40, C53, C54). OpenEval rates summary claims as SUPPORTED by collective evidence; peer R6 addresses oxytocin effects on SEI (C53) with UNCERTAIN rating due to consistency concerns.

OpenEval evaluated background/literature claims (C8, C21, C38, C41-C67) as SUPPORTED, noting they provide necessary context but are not novel findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval rated hypotheses and mechanistic speculation (C68-C70, C76-C77) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are plausible but not directly tested with no neural data presented. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rated inference about individual differences (C75) as SUPPORTED but noted it is speculative extrapolation about future research rather than direct finding. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
